question: HS's CAD-based joint check puts SO-101's shoulder at 80% of its 7.4 V STS3215's stall torque unloaded and 136% with 150 g. Do SO-100/SO-101 owners report shoulder or servo overloads?

hs_prediction.rule: HS requires under 50% of stall with a 1.5 safety factor

evidence.quote: the shoulder_lift motor (#2) of the SO100 robot experiences intermittent overloads and disconnects. The issue occurs even when other motors are functioning normally.
evidence.reply: A maintainer suggested a faulty motor and swapping it to another joint; the issue has no resolution posted.

evidence.quote: I've been seeing the gears strip when there is a stall of over 15% of the max torque limit (which works out to a max of 4.5 kg cm).
evidence.also: the same builder reports three burned-out servos; joint not named

evidence.quote: Under realistic heavy moves (multiple joints accelerating or holding near stall), the bus can brown-out
evidence.note: a supply concern, not a joint measurement

evidence.finding: LeRobot limits torque and current only on the gripper (Max_Torque_Limit 500, Protection_Current 250); the shoulder runs unlimited

result: Consistent with HS's warning, not proof of it: one shoulder-specific overload report, and a builder whose STS3215 gears strip at stalls above about 15% of rated torque, which makes HS's 50%-of-stall rule look lenient rather than strict. No report gives a measured shoulder torque or payload.
what_would_settle_it: Log STS3215 Present_Load on the SO-101 shoulder while holding the arm out with 0 g and 150 g; HS predicts about 80% and over 100% of stall.
